verdict.rationale: Bevy is free and open-source under MIT or Apache 2.0, which permits reading and modifying the code, and it has a public GitHub repository. Its docs say this is deliberate: developers should 'fully own their tools' and have visibility into them. A crates.io probe confirms the MIT OR Apache-2.0 license, and a community comment praises the no-strings MIT license. Missing for 10: first-party guidance on the workflow for modifying or patching the engine source (e.g., forking or overriding the crate dependency).

support.subject: As a game developer, I can read and modify the full engine source when I hit a wall

citations.quote: It is free and open-source forever under your choice of the MIT or Apache 2.0 licenses.
The code is free and open-source because we believe developers should fully own their tools.
MIT License, well done! It's so refreshing to see things released with no strings attached
